title: NY State Assembly · District 84
area: South Bronx, including Mott Haven, Port Morris, Melrose and Longwood.

context.text: Incumbent Amanda Septimo also filed to run for the U.S. House in New York's 15th Congressional District in 2026 but did not appear on the ballot for the June 23 Democratic primary; she instead sought re-election to her Assembly seat, defeating Hector Feliciano and Courtland Hankins 59.6%-21.2%-18.6% in the Assembly Democratic primary. Tyreek Goodman, the Conservative Party nominee, ran unsuccessfully for New York City Council District 8 in 2025 (12.0% on the Republican/Conservative line) and previously ran against Septimo for this Assembly seat in 2024 (2.9% on the Conservative line).

candidates.name: Amanda Septimo

summary.text: Amanda Septimo is the Democratic and Working Families Party nominee for re-election in NY Assembly District 84, a South Bronx seat she has held since January 2021. A lifelong Bronx resident, she serves on the Ways and Means, Education, Banks, Agriculture, Environmental Conservation and Veterans' Affairs committees.

background.text: A lifelong Bronx resident who began organizing in the South Bronx around social, economic and environmental issues as a teenager, working with The Point Community Development Corporation's youth activism program.
Received the Posse Scholarship, a full-tuition scholarship to Vanderbilt University, where she interned with the Legal Aid Society on domestic-violence cases and with Metro Public Defenders.
Worked for U.S. Rep. José E. Serrano as a community liaison and later as district director, and later worked with the Council of School Supervisors and Administrators (CSA).
Has served with the New York City Parks Department and the International YMCA.
First elected to the Assembly in 2020 after an earlier unsuccessful run for the seat; assumed office January 1, 2021.

Also sought the Democratic nomination for U.S. House in New York's 15th Congressional District in 2026 but did not appear on the June 23 primary ballot, and ran instead for re-election to her Assembly seat.

priorities.text: Fighting for affordable communities: tenant protections, economic opportunity and investments that help families stay in the neighborhoods they built.
Expanding healthcare access and opposing cuts to programs working families depend on.
Supporting safer neighborhoods through investments in violence prevention, mental health services and youth programs.
Investing in schools and young people, including better-funded schools, youth programs and childcare access.

positions.summary: Lists tenant protections among her priorities for making New York more affordable for working families.
As Essential Plan health-coverage cuts approached, joined advocates urging Governor Hochul to raise taxes on the wealthy, according to Bronx Times coverage referenced on her campaign site.
Describes herself as a strong advocate for affordable healthcare and community health resources, and has spoken out against proposed cuts to health-coverage programs including the Essential Plan.
Her campaign cites a 667-day stretch without gun violence at a NYCHA development in her district as part of her public-safety record, framed around violence-prevention investment.

record.text: Secured $6 million allocated for a new opioid treatment center at Lincoln Hospital.
Secured $6 million to combat the fentanyl crisis in the district, according to PIX11 coverage.
Sponsored new legislation aimed at tackling food insecurity through tax credits and reforms, according to News 12 Bronx coverage.
Donated $50,000 in discretionary funding to the Brides' March, an annual march against domestic violence.
Publicly opposed cuts to the Essential Plan and joined calls for Governor Hochul to raise taxes on high earners to offset the loss of coverage, per Bronx Times coverage.

candidates.researchNotes: Septimo has not completed a 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey. Her sponsored-legislation table on Ballotpedia is rendered via JavaScript and was not accessible to this research tool; record items instead draw on press coverage her own campaign site links to, which describe specific district investments and legislative actions but were not independently re-verified against the original news articles.

candidates.name: Tyreek Goodman

summary.text: Tyreek Goodman is the Conservative Party nominee for NY Assembly District 84. He has run for office twice before without success: for this Assembly seat in 2024 (2.9%) and for New York City Council District 8 in 2025 (12.0%). He has not held elected office.

background.text: Ran for NY Assembly District 84 in 2024 on the Conservative Party line, finishing third with 2.9% of the vote behind Amanda Septimo (D/WFP) and Rosaline Nieves (R).

Ran for New York City Council District 8 in the November 4, 2025 general election on the Republican and Conservative Party lines, finishing second with 12.0% of the vote (3,486 votes) behind Elsie Encarnacion.

candidates.researchNotes: No campaign website, Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey response, or public policy statements could be located for Goodman. His documented public record consists of his 2024 Assembly run and 2025 City Council run, both unsuccessful. He has not held elected office.
